newsitem.title: USA: US Justice official details radio merger criteria.
newsitem.headline: US Justice official details radio merger criteria.

text.p: A top U.S. Justice Department official said Wednesday that trustbusters would take a close look at any radio station mergers that give owners more than about one-third of market share in an area.

Acting antitrust division chief Joel Klein told the National Association of Brodcasters that market share was an important consideration in deciding whether to permit radio stations to acquire each other under the antitrust laws.

The speech was delivered one day after Evergreen Media Corp of Irving, Texas, announced it would buy Chancellor Broadcasting Co in a stock swap and then acquire 10 radio properties owned by Viacom Inc, creating a company worth about $5 billion.
Klein said that while there is no hard-and-fast rule, radio stations should be careful if acquisitions would give them more than about one-third of market share in an area.

"When you're doing a deal that's in the 35 percent and above range -- or that consolidates a large part of a particular format, even when that involves less than 35 percent of the overall market -- you should bring in antitrust counsel early on," he said.
Klein said the concern of the antitrust division was that radio stations would "raise prices for those customers who don't have other realistic options."
Klein said the government considers radio as a distinct market that must be governed by antitrust laws, even though it may have a small percentage of the overall advertising dollar.
"I can tell you from personal experience that if you think advertisers can always sell rock CDs as well through newspapers as through radio, you haven't had teenage kids," he said.
